clue.text: Book champion boxer?

blocks.note: first meaning: Tolkien's famous fantasy novel
second meaning, playful: the master of the boxing ring, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical reading: a boxing champion rules the rings he fights in.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's trilogy title also works as a jokey title for whoever dominates the boxing ring.

clue.text: You should be switched on by this

definitions.text: You should be switched on by this

blocks.clueFragment: You should be switched on by this
blocks.note: surface reading: a hint about getting someone motivated or alert
setter's reading: the hour after which motorists must turn their vehicle lamps on

explanation.surface: A deadline by which a person ought to be alert and keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' stands for your car's lamps; 'switched on' sounds like being keen, but it means lights coming on at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the official evening hour from which road vehicles must show their lamps.

clue.text: Savoury portion, not well cooked

blocks.note: meat that is underdone is rare
a bit is a small portion

explanation.surface: A small serving of something savoury that came out undercooked.
explanation.walkthrough: A rarebit (Welsh rarebit) is cheese on toast, a classic British savoury dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit, melted cheese on toast, is served as a savoury, a small salty course or snack.

clue.text: Blue and not feeling well

blocks.note: first meaning: risqué, smutty, as in a blue joke
second meaning: slightly unwell, under the weather

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like feeling sad, which suits the surface, but here it means rude or indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both slightly indecent humour and a person who is mildly ill.

clue.text: Article on lack of personal hygiene by doctor may be a deterrent

blocks.note: the definite article
BO stands for body odour
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about poor hygiene written by a doctor that might put people off.
explanation.walkthrough: The nuclear weapon is the classic deterrent, which makes the definition fair despite the hedging 'may be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear weapons, collectively the bomb, are held mainly as a deterrent against attack.

clue.text: Turn me over - that's better!

indicators.note: to turn something round is to flip its direction, so the little word me is read the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
something over is finished

explanation.surface: Someone being rolled over says it feels much better.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an exclamation: something emended has been corrected, which is to say made better.
explanation.definitionFit: Emended text has been corrected and improved, so the exclamation fits a successful revision.

clue.text: Test side batting needs help in upset

indicators.note: in a down entry, being upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a cricket side batting is in
aid means help

explanation.surface: A Test cricket team at the crease needs rescuing after a collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: Test with a capital means a Test match, international cricket between nations.
explanation.definitionFit: India is one of the nations that plays international Test cricket, so its team is a Test side.

clue.text: Turned into a dreadful tragedy

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the following word's letters are in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A situation that became a terrible disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to spin or revolve, so something that gyrated has turned round.

clue.text: Victorian expression of disapproval

blocks.note: surface reading: any prim frown from the nineteenth century
setter's reading: belonging to Queen Victoria herself, whose famous rebuke used the royal plural

explanation.surface: A prim nineteenth-century show of displeasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' means of Victoria personally: the quotation is attributed to the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria is famously credited with this frosty royal-plural put-down of an improper joke.

clue.text: An animal unlikely to be overlooked

definitions.text: An animal unlikely to be overlooked

blocks.note: surface reading: a creature too conspicuous to be ignored
setter's reading: literally looked over, which is hard when the beast is taller than anyone

explanation.surface: A creature so conspicuous nobody fails to notice it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tallest land mammal is almost impossible for anyone to see over the top of.

clue.text: Back possibly sore after the finish

indicators.note: possibly hints at one of several arrangements, so the word sore may be rearranged

blocks.note: the end is the finish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner's back may be aching once the race is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' sounds like the body part, but it is a verb meaning to support.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or plan is to support it publicly, a common sense of back.

clue.text: Label a pair socially unacceptable

blocks.note: a tab is a small label
a pair of round letters, like two noughts

explanation.surface: Branding a couple as social outcasts.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair is a pair of O's, two zeros side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden by custom, outside what polite society tolerates.

clue.text: One who used to teach painting

blocks.note: first meaning, playful: a former schoolmaster, a master of old
second meaning: a canvas by a great European artist before about 1800

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a retired art teacher; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A great pre-modern European painter, or a work by one, is called this, and literally it is a teacher from the past.

clue.text: Fair assessment of those not beyond redemption

definitions.text: Fair assessment of those not beyond redemption

blocks.note: surface reading: a just verdict on people who can still be saved
setter's reading: a middling grade, the kind of mild verdict given to someone passable

explanation.surface: A just judgment passed on sinners who might yet be saved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' seems to mean just, but it means middling: the phrase is a mild verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is passable or fairly decent is the mild verdict you give a person still worth saving.

clue.text: He sculpted a man embracing a girl

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the man's name wraps around the girl's

blocks.note: Ron is a man's name
Di is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An artist carved a couple in an embrace, as in The Kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: Rodin's most famous sculpture, The Kiss, shows exactly this, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French artist behind The Thinker and The Kiss.

clue.text: Occupiers who pay neither top nor bottom in rents

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the following word

blocks.note: what is neither top nor bottom is a side
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tenants who are charged neither the highest nor the lowest rents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who pay' only dresses the surface; the definition is just the first word, and 'neither top nor bottom' describes a position rather than an amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents are the people living in and occupying a building or place.

clue.text: Show into Poe's house?

blocks.note: first meaning: to lead someone to a seat or room
second meaning: Edgar Allan Poe's tale The Fall of the House of ...

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the house is fictional: the family house in Poe's story.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher is to escort someone in, and Usher is the doomed family in Poe's famous horror tale.

clue.text: Finding cannabis will settle his hash

indicators.note: to settle things is to sort them out, so the following words' letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drug find will put an end to someone's mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: To settle someone's hash is an idiom for putting him firmly in his place; hash is also slang for the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Hashish is the resin extracted from the cannabis plant, smoked as a drug.

clue.text: The means I contrived to control the sail

definitions.note: names the job; the answer is the rope that does it

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially devised, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor explains how they rigged a way to manage the canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: On a yacht the mainsheet is the line used to trim the angle of the mainsail.

clue.text: Broods about one's exploits

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the next piece

blocks.note: to muse is to brood or ponder
one is I, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Someone dwells gloomily on their own daring deeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploits' looks like a noun for feats, but it is a verb meaning takes unfair advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: To misuse something is to use it wrongly, as one who unfairly exploits a person or resource does.

clue.text: It's specifically used by diabetics

blocks.note: surface reading: anything made specially for people with diabetes, such as sugar-free food
setter's reading: the one treatment that is specific to the condition, injected daily

explanation.surface: A product designed especially for people with diabetes.
explanation.definitionFit: This hormone regulates blood sugar and is injected by many people whose bodies make too little of it.

clue.text: Green damaged after record stand

indicators.note: damaged things are knocked out of shape, so the letters of green are rearranged

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
taken as written

explanation.surface: A green turntable or display stand was broken after a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: An epergne is an ornamental centrepiece for a dining table, with dishes or vases on branching arms.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is a decorative tiered stand holding fruit or flowers in the middle of a table.

clue.text: Experiment on patients may set precedents

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: patients, or cases, used for a trial
second meaning: legal actions whose rulings guide later judgments

explanation.walkthrough: Doctors call patients cases, so cases being tested is the first reading; the second is the legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawsuits brought to establish a principle are called this, and patients under trial are literally cases tested.

clue.text: The nerve of the chap

blocks.note: first meaning: impudence, audacity
second meaning: an old word for the jaw or side of the face

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap' looks like a man, but it is the old word for the jaw or cheek, as in Bath chaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent boldness is called this, and it is also the fleshy side of the face, which chap once meant.

clue.text: Ideal leader for daily paper

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of daily
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: The perfect front-page story for a daily newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' and 'daily paper' suggest a newspaper editorial, but they split into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream as an adjective or noun means a perfect, ideal thing, as in a dream house.

clue.text: Girls get degrees without a study

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the degrees go around the rest

blocks.note: MAs are Master of Arts degrees
a, meaning one, is the Roman numeral I
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Young women earn their degrees without studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but it is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidens is an old-fashioned or poetic word for young unmarried women.

clue.text: I get new angles about payments for newspaper articles

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A journalist pitches fresh slants on stories about how freelance writers are paid.
explanation.walkthrough: Linage is payment for journalism calculated by the number of lines printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Freelance reporters were traditionally paid by the line, and these per-line fees are called linage.

clue.text: Gives no indication

blocks.note: surface reading: shows no sign of anything at all
setter's reading: signals the word no, by a sideways motion of the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives no indication' sounds like revealing nothing, but it means signalling 'no' without speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning the head from side to side is the gesture that signals refusal or disagreement.
